title: The reactor meant to showcase nuclear’s comeback keeps hitting problems
gist: The NRC warned Holtec International about a "chilled work environment" at the Palisades plant in Michigan, the flagship US reactor restart. The warning followed a worker falling into the reactor cavity, a fuel bundle tilting during refuelling and nine of 15 operator candidates failing licensing exams. It comes as more than $30 billion has been wiped off five US-listed nuclear stocks and Holtec has postponed a $900 million IPO, with a March 2027 deadline to begin supplying power.

themes.theme: NRC warning and safety incidents at Palisades

insights.claim: The US Nuclear Regulatory Commission told Holtec International to address a "chilled work environment" at the Palisades nuclear plant in Michigan, where staff are hesitant to raise safety concerns for fear of retaliation. The NRC will review Holtec's corrective plan within 30 days.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Regulatory scrutiny of the flagship restart adds schedule risk to the US nuclear-revival story.

insights.claim: At Palisades, a contractor fell into the reactor cavity and ingested water, with 300 counts per minute of radiation detected in their hair after decontamination. In August a bundle of nuclear fuel rods tilted over during refuelling, which delayed what was expected to be the first US reopening of a shuttered reactor.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Operational mishaps during the restart point to execution risk for first-of-a-kind reactor restarts.

insights.claim: Nine of the 15 reactor operator candidates at Palisades failed the initial licence examination given in July and August, and only six were issued operator licences.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: A shortage of licensed operators could limit restart timelines across the industry, not just at Palisades.

insights.claim: The NRC played down any immediate public risk at Palisades, saying mitigating measures ensured plant safety was not compromised. Holtec said the tilted fuel assembly was recovered without spilling and that the injured worker had minor injuries and quickly returned to work.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: With no immediate safety finding, a shutdown-level outcome is unlikely and the risk is mainly to the schedule.
insights.quote: “The assertion that we have rushed has directly been countered by the work that has been accomplished.”

themes.theme: Political and financial pressure on the nuclear revival

insights.claim: Critics fear that financial and political pressure to revive nuclear power as an answer to booming AI-driven electricity demand is increasing the risk of accidents, as the Trump administration cuts regulation and promises to reverse a culture of "risk aversion" at the NRC.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: A serious incident could reverse the policy tailwind for nuclear, a tail risk for nuclear equities that depend on AI power demand.
insights.locator: The warning has prompted concerns among

insights.claim: Former NRC chair Allison Macfarlane said Holtec is a newcomer to operating power plants and may be under heavy financial and political pressure to restart Palisades quickly, reflecting a "move fast and break things" culture in part of the industry, whereas nuclear safety requires going slowly and carefully.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Expert criticism raises the chance that regulators push back on fast-tracked projects.
insights.quote: But to ensure safety, nuclear needs a culture based on going slowly and carefully.

insights.claim: The Trump administration promotes nuclear energy as an edge in the AI race against China, has cut regulation and provided tens of billions of dollars in funding to speed up projects.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Federal subsidies are a key driver of nuclear project economics.

insights.claim: Holtec, which has never operated a nuclear power plant, has secured about $2.2 billion in government support for Palisades, including a $1.5 billion Department of Energy loan in 2024. Its customers secured an extra $1.3 billion in government funds to buy power from the plant.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Large public financing ties taxpayer exposure to Holtec's ability to deliver the restart.

insights.claim: Holtec faces a March 2027 contractual deadline to start supplying power from Palisades to customers.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: The March 2027 date is the key milestone; missing it would hurt Holtec's credibility as an operator.

insights.claim: Last month Holtec postponed a planned IPO that was expected to raise $900 million and value the New Jersey-based company at up to $10 billion.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: The delayed IPO is a sign that the market for nuclear listings is closing.

insights.claim: Holtec, which is trying to move from supplying nuclear components and services to designing reactors and operating plants, has faced a whistleblower lawsuit and legal disputes with former executives over alleged financial misrepresentation, executive retaliation and fraudulent practices. Founder and CEO Kris Singh has rejected the claims.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Governance issues add to the risk for any future Holtec IPO.

themes.theme: Fading investor appetite for nuclear stocks

insights.claim: More than $30 billion has been wiped off the value of five of the largest US-listed nuclear energy companies (Oklo, Centrus Energy, BWX Technologies, NuScale and Nano Nuclear) in the last year, as investor interest faded on concerns that the AI boom is slowing.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Nuclear equities are trading as a proxy for AI power demand, and that link is now working in reverse.

insights.claim: Soon after Palisades began restart work, the owners of two other plants slated for decommissioning, Three Mile Island in Pennsylvania and Duane Arnold in Iowa, announced restarts.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Problems at Palisades are a read-across risk for the other restart projects.
